title: DARPA program sets distance record for power beaming
readingDepth: Full short agency release, particularly paragraphs on distance/power and efficiency.
claim: DARPA reports more than 800 W delivered during a 30-second transmission over 8.6 km. The greater-than-20% efficiency statement concerns shorter-distance optical-input to electrical-output measurements.
limits: This release does not report wall-plug efficiency for the 8.6 km run or provide independent raw-data replication. Power comes from an externally powered laser.

title: U.S. Department of Energy Announces $10 Million in Funding to Projects Studying Low-Energy Nuclear Reactions
readingDepth: Official indexed title/date and search excerpt; direct HTML retrieved only a JavaScript shell. Article body not read.
claim: The official indexed release dated February 17, 2023 announces $10 million for eight research projects investigating LENR.
limits: Funding is not a physical result, disbursement audit, current project completion record or net-gain demonstration. The article body and final award reports were not acquired.
locator: Official indexed release title/date and search excerpt

title: MARRS: Mechanisms for Amplification of fusion Reaction Rates in Solids
readingDepth: Full program overview, including Exploring Advances, Why Fusion Matters and Exploring the Unknown.
claim: DARPA describes research into mechanisms that might increase fusion rates in solids; useful power is a conditional future application.
limits: Its cited evidence and replication claims remain attributed to DARPA; the underlying papers were not independently reproduced in this records task. No useful net-energy system is documented by the overview.
locator: Program overview, Exploring the Unknown; observed 2026-10-21

title: MARRS Broad Agency Announcement HR001126S0007
readingDepth: Downloaded original PDF; text read printed/PDF pages 1–8; printed/PDF page 4 visually inspected.
claim: The solicitation was posted December 30, 2025, with a March 12, 2026 proposal deadline; it requires falsifiable models and measurements. Page 4 contains a cross-section unit inconsistency: picobarn is paired with 10^-12 cm².
limits: Initial solicitation dates do not establish present award status. The literal unit inconsistency must not enter simulations: 1 pb = 10^-36 cm². This correction does not validate or refute the cited experiments.

title: HR001126S0007 MARRS Frequently Asked Questions, as of February 26, 2026
readingDepth: All five PDF pages opened; focused Q24, Q17, Q4 and Q3.
claim: The FAQ says calorimetry alone is insufficient; energy gain is a long-term vision rather than a program metric. A proposed brute-force route must still address trigger efficiency and a path to gain.
limits: These are proposal requirements, not evidence that any awardee attained gain. Reaction rates, calorimetry, and net system energy remain different quantities.
locator: Q24 p. 2, Q17 p. 3, Q4 and Q3 p. 5

title: Prospects for Breakthrough Propulsion From Physics
readingDepth: NTRS metadata and report abstract, overview, selected task summaries and Casimir discussion; PDF pp. 4–8.
claim: The report describes NASA support during 1996–2002 and classifies sixteen tasks from NASA and other sponsors as six nonviable, six unresolved/debatable, and four candidates for follow-up.
limits: This is a historical, bounded assessment. Follow-up opportunity is not a demonstrated space drive or energy source, and its bibliography is not automatically verified evidence.
locator: NTRS document 20040070788; printed pp. 1–5, especially p. 2 result counts

title: US685957A: Apparatus for the utilization of radiant energy
venue: U.S. patent, reproduced by Google Patents
status: historical granted patent; performance not independently verified here
readingDepth: Patent description, claims, metadata and figure descriptions read; original scan linked but not separately compared.
claim: Filed March 21 and granted November 5, 1901, the patent describes radiant input charging a capacitor. Its artificial-source variant also identifies a local current source.
limits: A patent grant does not validate claimed efficiency or modern microscopic explanations. Incoming radiation, initial stored energy, switches and any local supply belong in the budget. Aggregator legal-status labels are not a current legal opinion.
locator: Description of Figs. 1 and 3; claims; filing and grant metadata

title: Analysis and Assessment of Gateway Process
venue: Department of the Army; GovInfo archive
readingDepth: Official 29-page PDF downloaded; PDF pages 1, 7 and 28 OCR-read; pages 1 and 28 visually inspected. Selected passages only.
claim: The Army assessment is dated June 9, 1983 and bears a September 10, 2003 release stamp. Inspected passages discuss consciousness, resonance interpretations and proposed future exercises.
limits: The inspected passages provide no calibrated electrical-output, calorimetric or closed-cycle energy measurement. Government custody authenticates this record, not its physical interpretations; no conclusion about every related document is claimed.
